writeup: TIC 120025344 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.276805 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 3.19 percent dimming in the target's light, with a detection significance of 219.4 in the Box Least Squares periodogram. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the eclipse signal originates from the target location, though with a centroid offset of 1.3 arcseconds. A secondary eclipse was not detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued object. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true orbital period is double the initial automated finding - a data quality flag that requires attention when evaluating this candidate's properties.
